name: Gas cylinders (propane, CO2, air)
summary: Pressure cylinders for propane, butane, CO2, air and welding gases. Keep them upright and away from heat, and never cut or drill one, even when empty.
uses: Propane for cooking, heating and lights
CO2 and air for tyres and air tools
Running a generator converted to propane
identify: Propane bottles on grills, patio heaters, campers and forklifts (horizontal tanks), and in exchange cages outside shops; CO2 at bars, restaurants and paintball shops; air tanks at dive shops and fire stations. The collar is stamped with the gas, test date and empty weight (TW).
test: Weigh it and subtract the stamped empty weight to see what’s left. Check the valve and threads, and brush soapy water on joints: bubbles mean a leak.

decay.note: Cylinders hold gas for years; rusted or out-of-date ones may be unsafe to refill.
